change.title: pr-4
change.description: FEATURE: Embeddable Discourse comments, now with simple-rss instead of feedzirra
change.author: Robin Ward

findings.title: Protocol-relative links and images get the wrong host
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats any href/src starting with `/` as a path. A protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/a.png` matches that test, then `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so it becomes `http://<blog host>/cdn.example.com/a.png`. The same happens for `src` (line 71). Check for `//` before the single-slash case and keep the scheme. No spec covers this: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only uses `/hello` and `/images/wat.jpg`.
findings.originReason: absolutize_urls is new in this diff.

verification.reason: `start_with?('/')` also matches `//cdn.example.com/x`, and `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both slashes, so the result is `http://<host>/cdn.example.com/x`. The spec only uses single-slash paths.

findings.title: Feed content is stored as raw HTML and rendered without the sanitising pipeline
findings.body: `Post#cook` returns `raw` for `raw_html` posts, and every `TopicEmbed.import` sets that method (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22). The RSS path passes `CGI.unescapeHTML` output straight in (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35), so escaped markup in a feed becomes live HTML. The footer link is also interpolated unescaped into an href (app/models/topic_embed.rb:13). app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 prints `post.cooked` with `raw`, on the forum's own origin, for anonymous visitors. I did not verify how the forum client renders `cooked` on other pages. The Readability path (`import_remote`) is tag-whitelisted; the feed path is not. Fix: run feed bodies through the same sanitiser the cooking pipeline uses before storing them, and escape the footer link.
findings.originReason: The raw_html cook bypass and the import paths are added by this diff.

verification.reason: raw_html posts skip cooking (`cook` returns `raw`), and feed content is passed through CGI.unescapeHTML with no sanitising. The footer interpolates `url` unescaped inside a single-quoted href, and best.html.erb prints `cooked` with `raw`. A `'` is a valid URI character, so even an on-demand embed_url on the allowed host can break out of the attribute.

findings.title: Anonymous requests make the forum fetch and import any page on the embeddable host
findings.body: `best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any `embed_url` with no login requirement (line 15). The job fetches the URL (lib/topic_retriever.rb:45-52) and creates a topic from it as the embed user (app/models/topic_embed.rb:20-30). The gates are the same-host check (lib/topic_retriever.rb:15) and the referer check (line 26), which is a client-set header and not an access control. The 60-second throttle is keyed per URL (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-32), so a visitor can vary a query string to get a fetch and a new topic each time. The embed user's create limit is an after_create callback (lib/rate_limiter/on_create_record.rb:29-35), so `skip_validations` does not bypass it; once it is hit, `performed!` raises (lib/rate_limiter.rb:35-46) inside the job. Consider requiring a login for on-demand retrieval, or limiting by requester.

verification.reason: `best` enqueues retrieve_topic for any anonymous request that has a matching Referer. The throttle key is per embed_url, so changing the query string gives a new fetch and a new topic each time. The topic rate limit is an after_create callback that raises LimitExceeded in the job.

findings.title: One bad feed item aborts the whole feed import and blocks on-demand retrieval
findings.body: The loop (lines 31-37) has no per-item rescue. Three things can raise there: `i.content` is nil when an item has no content field, and line 35 calls `.scrub` on it (I believe simple-rss maps only content:encoded to `content`; not verified); a `TopicEmbed.import` that hits the embed user's create limit raises LimitExceeded (lib/rate_limiter.rb:46); and a DB error on a long or blank field. Every later item is then skipped until the next run. `perform_retrieve` calls `poll_feed` before `fetch_http` (lib/topic_retriever.rb:40-45), so an exception there also stops the on-demand import for the URL the visitor asked for. Rescue per item and log, and keep the HTTP fallback independent of the feed.
findings.originReason: PollFeed is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The item loop has no rescue. `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content, and any exception from TopicEmbed.import stops the remaining items. perform_retrieve calls PollFeed before fetch_http, so the same exception also aborts the HTTP fallback.

findings.title: A trashed embed topic or post is never recovered and breaks the embed
findings.body: TopicEmbed rows have no `dependent` handling (app/models/topic_embed.rb:4-5), and trashing a topic leaves the row in place. `topic_id_for_embed` still returns the id, then `TopicView.new` runs `find_topic`, which excludes deleted rows through Trashable's default scope (lib/topic_view.rb:260-264; lib/trashable.rb:5), and raises NotFound (lib/topic_view.rb:299-300). Every visitor gets a 404 for that URL. `perform_retrieve` returns at line 37 because the row exists, so nothing re-imports it. In the update path, a trashed post makes `embed.post` nil (app/models/topic_embed.rb:32), and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises (lines 35-36). Decide whether a trashed embed topic should be recreated, and handle a nil `embed.post`.
findings.originReason: The embed lookup and update path are new.

verification.reason: For non-staff users, TopicView#find_topic goes through Trashable's default scope, so a trashed topic is nil and raises NotFound. Meanwhile the TopicEmbed row still exists, so perform_retrieve bails out early. A trashed post makes `embed.post` nil, and PostRevisor#revise! then calls `nil.raw`.

findings.title: A failed retrieve leaves the embed on 'Loading' with no error
findings.body: When `embed_by_username` names no user, `fetch_http` returns silently (line 50). When the fetch raises (404, timeout, rate limit, DB error), the job fails with no record the visitor or admin can see. app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10 reloads the iframe every 30 seconds, and each reload enqueues another job (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15), so the page loads forever. Make a missing user a visible setting error, and give the view a failed state rather than an endless loader.
findings.originReason: Retriever and loading view are new.

verification.reason: fetch_http returns nil silently when there is no user, and any exception just fails the job. loading.html.erb reloads every 30 seconds with no failure state, so the visitor sees 'Loading' forever.

findings.title: The Disqus import changed behaviour without mention in the PR
findings.body: The `--category` option is removed from the declarations and its lookup deleted, so categories are silently no longer applied. The old `PostCreator` call passed `created_at`; the new call does not, so topics get the import time. The topic body changes from the permalink to an article fetched over HTTP (`import_remote`). `import` returns nil for a non-http link, and `if post.present?` (line 149) then silently skips every comment in that thread. A single fetch failure in `import_remote` (`open`) raises and stops the whole run. The PR body mentions none of this.
findings.originReason: The diff replaces the PostCreator call that passed created_at and category.

verification.reason: The diff removes the --category option and the `created_at:` argument, and replaces the permalink body with `import_remote`, which fetches over open() with no rescue. `import` returns nil for a non-http link, so `if post.present?` skips that thread's comments.

findings.title: force: true drops the table if it already exists
findings.body: `create_table ... force: true` drops and recreates `topic_embeds`. Under a normal `db:migrate` this is a no-op, but if the table exists with rows and the migration version was never recorded, the rows are lost. The embed_url-to-topic mapping cannot be rebuilt from other data. The same option on top_topics (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3) would drop derived data. Remove `force`, or check `table_exists?` first.

verification.reason: `force: true` drops an existing topic_embeds table before creating it. This only matters when the table exists but the migration was never recorded, so 'consider' is the right severity.

findings.title: An embed_url longer than the column limit makes the import fail
findings.body: `embed_url` is a `string` column with no explicit limit (db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:4). Under Rails 4 on PostgreSQL that is usually varchar(255); I did not verify this in the repo. Nothing checks the length of an incoming URL (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9; app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32). A longer URL makes `TopicEmbed.create!` (line 25) raise after the post was built in the transaction. The transaction rolls back, so no broken topic remains, but the job fails and, in the feed, the loop stops (see the poll-loop finding). Validate the length or widen the column.

verification.reason: `t.string :embed_url` has no limit, which is varchar(255) under Rails 4 on PostgreSQL, and nothing validates the URL length before `create!`, so an over-long URL raises. URLs that long are rare, so 'consider' fits better.

findings.title: Each unknown URL triggers a full feed download and re-import
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` before every HTTP fallback (lines 40-42). The 60-second throttle is per URL, not per feed, so N distinct unknown URLs cause N full feed downloads and N passes over every item, each re-hashed and re-parsed through `absolutize_urls`. `open(...)` in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 sets no timeout. Cache the feed poll for a window, or move it out of the request path.

verification.reason: Each perform_retrieve for an unknown URL runs PollFeed#execute, which downloads and re-imports the whole feed. The only throttle is per embed_url, and `open` sets no timeout.

findings.title: setnx and expire are two commands, so a crash can leave a key with no TTL
findings.body: `setnx` (line 27) and then `expire` (line 28) are separate commands. If the process dies between them, the key never expires, and `retrieved_recently?` returns true for that URL forever, so it is never retried. Use one atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` if the redis client version in use supports it.

verification.reason: setnx and expire are separate commands, so a crash between them leaves a key with no TTL, and that URL is then throttled forever. The bundled redis-rb 3.0.6 supports `set` with nx/ex.

findings.title: The origin check is a substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of the forum URL, not only an exact match. Compare `e.origin` with the forum's origin. The impact is limited to setting the iframe height.

verification.reason: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a prefix or substring of discourseUrl, such as `http://forum.ex` for `http://forum.example.com/`. The only impact is the iframe height.

findings.title: ALLOWALL is not a valid X-Frame-Options value
findings.body: Browsers accept DENY, SAMEORIGIN, or ALLOW-FROM and ignore other values, so this header has no effect and anyone can frame the embed page. The referer check is not a frame control. Use CSP `frame-ancestors` if framing should be limited, or drop the header. spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:37 asserts this value, so it must change with it.

verification.reason: ALLOWALL is not a standard X-Frame-Options value, and browsers ignore unknown values. In practice it only overrides Rails' SAMEORIGIN default and allows framing, which looks like the intent, so the impact is informational.

findings.title: 'is 404 without an embed_url' does not test the missing parameter
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` runs first. With the default `embeddable_host` of '' (config/site_settings.yml:354), the request raises InvalidAccess before `params.require` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:9) runs. The test passes for the wrong reason and never checks for a 404. Set the host and referer in the test, then check the missing-parameter response.

verification.reason: The default embeddable_host is '', so the ensure_embeddable before_filter raises InvalidAccess before `params.require` runs. The test only asserts not-success, so it passes without ever exercising the missing-parameter path.

findings.title: No coverage for the feed import, the URL rewrite, or the throttle
findings.body: poll_feed_spec only covers the gating in `execute`. `poll_feed`, its per-item import, and an item with missing content are untested. spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb does not cover protocol-relative URLs. `retrieved_recently?`, `perform_retrieve` and `fetch_http` in spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb are only exercised with stubs, and RetrieveTopic has no spec. Line 2 (`require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`) is unrelated to this spec.

verification.reason: poll_feed_spec only covers execute's gating. topic_retriever_spec stubs perform_retrieve and retrieved_recently?. There is no RetrieveTopic spec, and topic_embed_spec only uses single-slash paths.

findings.title: Dead code: feed_key, and an unused permalink string
findings.body: `feed_key` (lines 20-22) is never called; nothing in the repo references it. `embed.permalink` in config/locales/server.en.yml:37 has no caller (a grep for `embed.` finds none). Remove both, or use them.

verification.reason: A grep finds `feed_key` only at its definition, and the `embed.permalink` key has no caller. The other embed keys are used.

findings.title: Adding a NOT NULL column with a default rewrites the whole posts table
findings.body: On PostgreSQL before 11, `add_column ... default: 1, null: false` rewrites every row of posts under an exclusive lock, which can mean a long outage during deploy on a large forum. Consider adding the column nullable, backfilling in batches, then setting NOT NULL. The default (1) maps to :regular via Enum (lib/enum.rb:10-16); I checked that.

verification.reason: On PostgreSQL versions before 11, `add_column` with a NOT NULL default rewrites the whole posts table under an exclusive lock.

findings.title: skip_validations also skips the uncategorized and title checks on embed topics
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` passes `skip_validations: true` to PostCreator (line 22). That reaches `Topic#save(validate: false)` (lib/topic_creator.rb:78), which skips the category-presence rule for uncategorized topics (app/models/topic.rb:58-62) and the title checks (app/models/topic.rb:49-53). Embedded topics are then created even where the site disallows uncategorized topics. Is that intended? If not, skip only what the import needs.

verification.reason: `skip_validations` makes TopicCreator call `save(validate: !skip_validations)`, which skips the title validators and the uncategorized category_id rule for embed topics.

contracts.action: GET /embed/best renders up to five best posts of an existing embed topic
contracts.before_after: Existing TopicView path with options {best: 5}, passing current_user as the topic page does. Nothing runs before the call except the ensure_embeddable before_filter, which is new.
contracts.visible_effect: The iframe shows best posts printed from post.cooked and links back to the topic.
contracts.failure_mode: A trashed topic makes find_topic return nil, so TopicView raises NotFound and the visitor gets a 404 for that URL. The TopicEmbed row stays, so the embed never recovers.

contracts.action: Anonymous request for an unknown embed_url enqueues retrieve_topic
contracts.before_after: The sibling enqueues jobs after the DB transaction commits, so the job sees the data. This request enqueues with no transaction, and nothing throttles the enqueue itself: each request for an unknown URL enqueues again, and the throttle only applies once the job runs.
contracts.visible_effect: The loading page is shown and reloads every 30 seconds.
contracts.failure_mode: If the job raises, or fetch_http returns early (missing user), nothing is shown and the loader repeats forever (lib/topic_retriever.rb:49-50; app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:8-10).

contracts.action: TopicRetriever calls PollFeed#execute inline before the HTTP fallback
contracts.before_after: The scheduled entry point runs hourly with retry disabled (poll_feed.rb:12). The inline call runs inside the RetrieveTopic job, after the existence check (topic_retriever.rb:37), before fetch_http (line 45), and re-checks the embed afterwards (line 42). Nothing bounds the total time: the feed open (poll_feed.rb:29) and the page open (app/models/topic_embed.rb:48) set no explicit timeout, and they run one after the other. The visitor does not wait because the job is asynchronous.
contracts.visible_effect: The loading page is shown for the whole duration.
contracts.failure_mode: No rescue. An exception from poll_feed propagates out of perform_retrieve, so fetch_http never runs for the requested URL.

contracts.action: Create a topic and first post from remote content, stored as raw_html
contracts.before_after: A normal post goes through cook(raw) in before_create_tasks (lib/post_creator.rb:105), which runs the rendering pipeline. This path sets cook_method (lib/post_creator.rb:216), so cook returns raw (app/models/post.rb:133). The pipeline, post_analyzer and the after_post_cook plugin filter are skipped.
contracts.visible_effect: cooked equals raw, so the markup from the feed is what the page prints.
contracts.failure_mode: Unsanitised HTML from the feed is stored and printed with raw (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19), on the forum origin, for anonymous visitors.

contracts.action: Update the embed post when content_sha1 changes
contracts.before_after: A normal revise! checks the edit rate limiter (lib/post_revisor.rb:53) and runs validations. This path passes bypass_rate_limiter and skip_validations (lib/post_revisor.rb:84-85) and does not pass bypass_bump, so each feed change bumps the topic (lib/post_revisor.rb:54-59). The sha is updated with update_column even if revise! returned false.
contracts.visible_effect: The post text changes and the topic moves to the top of its list.
contracts.failure_mode: If embed.post is nil (trashed post), PostRevisor.new(nil) raises inside the feed poll, and the whole loop stops.

contracts.action: Post#cook returns raw for raw_html posts
contracts.before_after: The normal branch runs post_analyzer.cook and the after_post_cook plugin filter. The new branch returns raw before either runs.
contracts.visible_effect: No markdown, no oneboxes, and no plugin cook filter for these posts.
contracts.failure_mode: Plugins that rely on after_post_cook do not see these posts.
contracts.open_question: Does anything that reads post_analyzer results (mentions, links, image counts) rely on cook running for these posts?

contracts.action: Disqus import creates the topic from the thread link
contracts.before_after: Before: PostCreator with a permalink raw, created_at and category. After: TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the page over HTTP and stores the extracted article. import returns nil for a non-http link, and then no comments from that thread are created.
contracts.visible_effect: Imported topics contain the article, not the permalink. Category and creation date are no longer set.
contracts.failure_mode: A non-http link, or a failed fetch, drops the thread's comments silently (line 149) or stops the run (open raises).

contracts.action: embed.js inserts the iframe and listens for resize messages
contracts.before_after: No existing path to compare. The script assumes #discourse-comments exists and that the global discourseUrl ends with a slash.
contracts.visible_effect: The iframe is added and its height follows the discourse-resize messages.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing #discourse-comments element throws at line 12 and shows nothing. The origin check at line 17 is a substring match.

contracts.action: Embed layout posts its height to the parent frame
contracts.before_after: No existing path. Sent once on window.onload, so height changes after load are not reported.
contracts.visible_effect: The iframe height matches the content at load time.
contracts.failure_mode: If the parent does not listen for the message, the iframe keeps its default height. No error is shown.

contracts.action: Migration adds posts.cook_method with default 1, NOT NULL
contracts.before_after: Enum starts at 1, so :regular is 1 and existing posts keep the normal pipeline. Checked.
contracts.failure_mode: On PostgreSQL before 11, the table is rewritten under a lock during deploy.

contracts.action: Anonymous embed responses are cached for one minute
contracts.before_after: discourse_expires_in applies only to anonymous visitors and passes the request to the anonymous cache for one minute. The loading page is cached too, and it reloads every 30 seconds.
contracts.visible_effect: A visitor can see the loading page up to a minute after the topic is created.
contracts.open_question: How does anon_cache key and store the response, and does it cache the loading view?

contracts.action: PostCreator rolls back silently when the topic save fails, so import returns nil
contracts.before_after: Normal callers read creator.errors. The import never reads errors: a Rollback is caught by the transaction, create returns nil, and import returns nil with no error.
contracts.visible_effect: None. The feed item is not imported and nothing is logged.
contracts.failure_mode: Feed items are dropped silently when topic validation fails.

summary: Reviewed all 28 files in part 1 (no binaries or unreadable files). I read the core code in full (topic_embed, embed_controller, topic_retriever, poll_feed, retrieve_topic, post, post_creator, post_revisor, disqus.thor and the migrations) and traced callees (TopicView, Trashable, RateLimiter, TopicCreator, Enum). Nothing was built or run. Findings: 9 "fix" and 10 "consider". The most serious are: feed HTML stored and rendered unsanitised (post.rb:133); anonymous requests can make the forum fetch and import arbitrary pages on the embeddable host (embed_controller.rb:15); one bad feed item aborts the whole feed import (poll_feed.rb:35); protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the wrong host (topic_embed.rb:65); and the Disqus importer changed behaviour without mention (disqus.thor:148). Items I could not verify here: simple-rss's `content` mapping, open-uri's load order at boot, the Rails 4 varchar default for embed_url, and how the forum client renders `cooked` outside this part. The Enum default for cook_method checks out (regular = 1).
